breakfast.name: Kaiserschmarrn (Emperor's Shredded Pancake)
instructions: Beat yolks with milk, sugar, salt; stir in flour
Beat whites to stiff peaks, fold in gently — this is what makes it fluffy
Melt butter in skillet, pour in batter
Add raisins if using
Cook until bottom sets, tear into pieces with two forks
Keep tossing and turning pieces until golden and caramelized
Dust generously with powdered sugar
Serve with warm plum compote
breakfast.description: Legend says Emperor Franz Joseph loved this torn-up pancake. Every ski hut and mountain restaurant in Austria serves it.

breakfast.name: Semmel mit Butter und Marmelade
instructions: Slice Semmeln in half
Spread generously with butter
Top with apricot jam
breakfast.description: The Austrian breakfast standard — a crusty roll, butter, and Wachau apricot jam. Eaten at every hotel breakfast table.

breakfast.name: Topfenpalatschinken (Curd-Filled Crêpes)
ingredients: Crêpes: 150g flour, 2 eggs, 250ml milk, pinch salt, butter
Filling: 500g Topfen (quark/curd cheese), 2 egg yolks, 60g sugar, lemon zest, vanilla, raisins
instructions: Make thin crêpes
Mix Topfen with yolks, sugar, lemon zest, vanilla, raisins
Fill each crêpe, roll up
Place in buttered baking dish, pour sour cream over
Bake at 180°C for 20 min
Dust with powdered sugar
breakfast.description: Delicate crêpes stuffed with sweetened curd cheese and baked until golden.

lunch.name: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: Clarified butter or lard for frying
instructions: Pound veal between plastic wrap until very thin and even
Season with salt only — never pepper on a Schnitzel
Dredge in flour, shake off excess
Dip in egg wash, let excess drip
Press into breadcrumbs — don't pack, keep it loose
Fry in plenty of hot fat — the Schnitzel must swim, not sit
Shake the pan constantly — this creates the signature wrinkly, puffy coating
Fry 2-3 min per side until deep golden
Drain briefly, serve immediately with lemon wedge
Parsley, lingonberry jam, and potato salad on the side
lunch.description: Vienna's gift to the world. Real Wiener Schnitzel is VEAL, never pork (that's Schnitzel Wiener Art). The coating must puff away from the meat.

lunch.name: Tafelspitz (Boiled Beef)
ingredients: Accompaniments: apple-horseradish sauce, chive sauce, roasted potatoes
instructions: Place bones in cold water, bring to boil, skim thoroughly
Add charred onion, peppercorns, bay leaf
After 1 hour, add the beef in one piece
Simmer very gently — never boil — for 2 hours
Add root vegetables in the last 45 min
Meat is done when a fork slides in and out easily
Slice against the grain, arrange on warm platter with vegetables
Serve in broth, with apple-horseradish and chive sauce alongside
Ladle some broth over the meat at the table
lunch.description: Emperor Franz Joseph's favorite meal, served daily at the Habsburg court. The test of a great Viennese cook.

lunch.name: Frittatensuppe (Pancake Strip Soup)
ingredients: Crêpes: 2 eggs, 100g flour, 150ml milk, salt, butter
instructions: Make thin crêpes, let cool
Roll each crêpe up tightly
Slice into thin strips (Frittaten)
Heat beef broth until piping hot
Place a nest of crêpe strips in each bowl
Ladle hot broth over
Scatter with chives
lunch.description: The classic first course of any Austrian Sunday lunch — delicate crêpe strips floating in crystal-clear beef broth.

dinner.name: Backhendl (Fried Chicken, Viennese-Style)
instructions: Season chicken with salt, rest 10 min
Coat in flour, egg, breadcrumbs — same technique as Schnitzel
Fry in plenty of hot fat, turning occasionally
Cook 12-15 min until deep golden and cooked through
Fry parsley sprigs briefly until crispy
Drain chicken on wire rack
Serve with lemon and fried parsley
dinner.description: Fried chicken, Austrian-style — crumbed like a Schnitzel. Predates American fried chicken by centuries.

dinner.name: Schweinsbraten (Roast Pork)
instructions: Score the skin in a diamond pattern
Rub salt and caraway into the cuts, stud with garlic
Place on rack in roasting pan with onion and beer
Roast at 180°C for 2 hours, basting with pan juices
Last 20 min, increase to 220°C for crackling
The skin should be shattering-crisp, the meat tender
Let rest 15 min
Serve with sauerkraut and bread dumplings, ladle pan juices over
dinner.description: Austrian-style pork roast with caraway and crackling — the Sunday dinner across Gasthaus kitchens.

dinner.name: Kaspressknödel (Cheese Dumplings)
instructions: Soak bread in milk until soft
Mix with eggs, cheese, sautéed onion, parsley, seasoning
Shape into thick patties (not balls)
Fry in butter until golden on both sides, 4 min per side
Serve floating in clear broth, or on a green salad with vinaigrette
dinner.description: Tyrolean cheese dumplings — pressed flat and fried golden, served in broth or on salad in every mountain hut.

snacks.name: Leberkäse-Semmel
instructions: Slice Leberkäse thick from the loaf — ideally fresh from the oven with a crispy top
Split Semmel
Place Leberkäse inside
Add mustard — the sweet Bavarian type is traditional
snacks.description: Austria's ubiquitous snack — a thick slab of warm meatloaf in a crusty roll with mustard. Bought from every Fleischerei and market stand.

snacks.name: Brezn (Pretzel)
ingredients: Lye bath: 1L water, 40g food-grade lye (or 60g baking soda)
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water with sugar
Mix with flour, salt, butter; knead until smooth and elastic
Rise 1 hour
Divide into 8 pieces, roll into long ropes
Shape into pretzels
Dip briefly in lye bath
Place on lined tray, sprinkle coarse salt
Bake at 220°C for 12-15 min until deep mahogany
snacks.description: Soft, chewy, lye-dipped pretzels with coarse salt — the Bäckerei staple.

snacks.name: Käsekrainer (Cheese-Filled Sausage)
ingredients: 2 Käsekrainer sausages (pork sausages with pockets of melted cheese inside)
instructions: Grill or pan-fry Käsekrainer until the skin is crispy and the cheese inside is molten
Be careful — the cheese explodes when you bite in
Serve in a Semmel roll with sweet mustard and horseradish
Or eat standalone at a Würstelstand (sausage stand)
snacks.description: Sausage with pockets of molten cheese inside — the Würstelstand (sausage stand) classic. Went viral when food tourists discovered the cheese explosion on the first bite. Available at 3am outside every Viennese nightclub.

desserts.name: Sachertorte
ingredients: Cake: 130g dark chocolate, 130g butter, 100g powdered sugar, 6 eggs (separated), 130g sugar, 130g flour
instructions: Melt chocolate, cool slightly
Cream butter and powdered sugar until fluffy
Add yolks one at a time, fold in melted chocolate
Beat whites with sugar to stiff peaks
Fold whites and flour alternately into chocolate mixture — gently
Bake at 175°C for 45 min, test with skewer
Cool, slice horizontally into two layers
Warm apricot jam, brush over top and sides, let set
Make glaze: boil sugar and water to thread stage (106°C), stir in chopped chocolate until smooth
Pour glaze over cake, spread evenly with palette knife — one smooth coat, no re-touching
Let set at room temperature
Serve with unsweetened whipped cream (Schlagobers) — never with the cake, always on the side
desserts.description: Hotel Sacher's legendary chocolate cake, the subject of a 7-year legal battle with Demel. The 'Original Sachertorte' stamp on top is a trademark.

desserts.name: Apfelstrudel (Apple Strudel)
ingredients: Strudel dough: 250g flour, 1 egg, 2 tbsp oil, warm water, pinch salt
Filling: 1kg tart apples (peeled, thin-sliced), 80g sugar, cinnamon, 80g raisins (rum-soaked), 80g breadcrumbs (toasted in butter), lemon zest
instructions: Make dough: mix flour, egg, oil, salt, water; knead until silky
Rest covered 30 min
Stretch dough on floured cloth by hand — pull from underneath with backs of hands until you can read a newspaper through it
Brush with melted butter
Spread toasted breadcrumbs, then apple slices, raisins, sugar, cinnamon, lemon zest
Roll up using the cloth, tuck ends under
Transfer to lined tray, brush with butter
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 min, brushing with butter twice more
Dust with powdered sugar while warm
Serve with warm vanilla sauce
desserts.description: Real Viennese strudel is hand-stretched paper-thin — bakery students must prove they can read through the dough. The breadcrumb layer keeps it crispy.

desserts.name: Buchteln (Jam-Filled Buns)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 250ml warm milk, 7g yeast, 80g sugar, 80g butter, 2 egg yolks, lemon zest, vanilla, pinch salt
Vanilla sauce (Vanillesoße): milk, vanilla, egg yolks, sugar, cornstarch
instructions: Make enriched dough, knead until silky, rise 1 hour
Divide into portions, flatten each, place a spoonful of plum jam in center
Close dough around jam, pinch shut, place seam-down in buttered pan — pack tightly together
Let rise 20 min
Bake at 180°C for 22-25 min until golden on top
Make vanilla sauce while they bake: heat milk with vanilla, whisk yolks with sugar and cornstarch, temper, cook until thick
Serve warm Buchteln — pull apart from each other — and drown in vanilla sauce
The jam inside should be molten
desserts.description: Soft yeast buns filled with plum jam, pulled apart at the table and drowned in hot vanilla sauce — Viennese grandmother food that went viral for the ASMR of pulling the connected buns apart. The vanilla sauce pooling around the warm buns is everything.

drinks.name: Wiener Melange
instructions: Brew strong coffee
Steam milk and create light foam
Pour coffee into cup, leaving room
Add steamed milk until cup is three-quarters full
Top with a cap of light foam
Serve with a glass of water on the side — always
drinks.description: Vienna's signature coffee — similar to a cappuccino but gentler. The glass of tap water served alongside is non-negotiable Viennese tradition.

drinks.name: Almdudler
instructions: Serve chilled
Austria's national soft drink — herbal and lightly sweet
Often mixed with white wine as a Spritzer (Almspritzer)
drinks.description: The Austrian answer to Coca-Cola — a herbal lemonade since 1957, outselling all other soft drinks in the country.

drinks.name: Glühwein (Mulled Wine)
instructions: Pour wine into pot, add all spices and orange peel
Heat gently — never boil, or the alcohol evaporates
Add sugar, stir until dissolved
Steep 15 min on low heat
Strain into mugs
Add a splash of rum if it's very cold outside
drinks.description: The smell of Christmas markets — warm spiced wine from November through December at every Christkindlmarkt stall in Austria.
